positions.position: PR description claims 'Update things_advanced.py to add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the actual change replaces req.stream.read() with req.bounded_stream.read() (no argument). This is a mismatch between description and code that suggests either the description is stale or the wrong change was committed.

Using req.bounded_stream is arguably the better fix because it works for both WSGI and ASGI and respects Content-Length implicitly; the description is simply out of date. Reviewer should ask the author to reconcile the description with the code, but the code change itself is defensible.

The PR title is about adding POST tests for things_advanced. The README.rst diff is large and unrelated: it reformats code, changes resp.status to falcon.code_to_http_status(), changes a handler signature (handle(ex, req, resp, params) -> handle(req, resp, ex, params)), and switches stream to bounded_stream. These changes do not belong in this PR and should be split.

Keeping README in sync with examples/things_advanced.py is reasonable since the example is the canonical source. Bundling the cosmetic refactor avoids drift. The signature change for StorageError.handle is a real API correction that aligns with falcon's error handler signature and is worth shipping together.

The FAQ example reads req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0). If content_length is None this passes 0 to read(), which returns b'' regardless of the actual body — masking real bodies sent without Content-Length. The example is teaching a subtly wrong pattern.
The FAQ example is just demonstrating how to override headers in tests; the resource logic is illustrative. Over-engineering it would distract from the FAQ's actual purpose.

issues.description: PR description does not match the actual code change in things_advanced.py
issues.detail: The PR description states the change adds 'req.content_length to req.stream.read()', but the diff actually changes 'req.stream.read()' to 'req.bounded_stream.read()' with no argument. This discrepancy suggests either the description is stale or the wrong change landed. Reviewer should clarify intent before merge so the changelog/news fragment is accurate.

issues.description: README.rst changes are out of scope for this PR
issues.detail: The PR title scopes work to test additions for things_advanced. README.rst receives a large refactor including a breaking-looking signature change (StorageError.handle parameter reorder from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params)), switching to falcon.code_to_http_status(), reformatting, and stream -> bounded_stream. These should be a separate PR so the test-only change can be reviewed independently and reverted cleanly if needed.

issues.description: FAQ example uses req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) which silently swallows bodies when Content-Length is missing
issues.detail: When content_length is None, 'req.content_length or 0' yields 0, so req.stream.read(0) returns b'' even if a body is present. This pattern is being taught in the FAQ as guidance and will be copy-pasted by readers. Either use req.bounded_stream.read() or read up to a sensible cap, and document the rationale.

issues.description: New test asserts only status code, not response body or side effects
issues.detail: test_things_advanced's new resp3 (201 path) checks only status_code; it does not verify that the Location header is set, the stored thing is retrievable, or that the JSON payload was actually parsed. Given the change moves from stream.read() to bounded_stream.read(), a test that asserts the body was successfully decoded into storage would be more meaningful for catching regressions in that exact code path.

issues.description: FAQ example class PostTest is not a valid pytest collection target but the name could confuse pytest
issues.detail: Classes prefixed with 'Test' (PostTest is fine since prefix doesn't match) are collected by pytest. PostTest avoids the collision, but using a name like 'EchoResource' or 'ContentLengthResource' would be clearer about intent in documentation. Minor stylistic nit.

issues.description: FAQ code block has minor Python style issues
issues.detail: The example uses 'headers = [(\'Content-Length\', \'1\'),]' with a trailing comma in a single-element list and 'assert(result.status == ...)' with parentheses around the assert expression (PEP 8 discourages this — assert is a statement not a function). For a docs example readers will copy, prefer 'headers = [(\'Content-Length\', \'1\')]' and 'assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400'.

issues.description: FAQ example missing blank line between class and decorator per PEP 8
issues.detail: The 'PostTest' class definition is immediately followed by '@pytest.fixture' with only one blank line. PEP 8 requires two blank lines between top-level definitions. Falcon's own contributing guidelines emphasize coding style consistency.

issues.description: News fragment not visible in diff despite checklist claiming one was added
issues.detail: The PR checklist claims a towncrier news fragment was added under docs/_newsfragments/ referencing issue #678, but no such file appears in the diff. Either the file is missing or it was not included in the diff context. Verify before merge.

issues.description: Test uses hard-coded user_id '1337' without explanation
issues.detail: tests/test_examples.py uses '/1337/things' as a path. While the existing GET test also uses this, a brief comment or a constant would aid readability — especially since the path includes a user_id segment that interacts with auth middleware.

issues.description: Author comments should be prefixed with GitHub nick per contributing guidelines
issues.detail: The PR checklist includes 'Prefixed code comments with GitHub nick and an appropriate prefix.' No new comments in this diff carry such a prefix, but no new comments were added that needed one. Informational — verify checklist accuracy.

review.summary: This PR has a reasonable core goal — add POST test coverage for the things_advanced example and document header overrides in the FAQ — but it suffers from scope creep and a mismatch between description and code. The largest concern is the unrelated README.rst refactor (including a handler signature reorder for StorageError.handle and stream -> bounded_stream changes) bundled into what should be a tests-only PR; this should be split. The PR description claims content_length is being passed to stream.read(), but the actual change switches to bounded_stream.read() with no argument — these need to be reconciled. The FAQ example teaches a subtly buggy pattern (req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) silently returns empty when Content-Length is missing) that readers will copy. The new tests assert only status codes, missing a chance to verify the bounded_stream behavior end-to-end. None of the issues are P0 blockers strictly, but the scope and FAQ correctness should be addressed before merge.
